conditioning.comment_epsilon: epsilon_t = ||A_t^{-1} Delta_t||_2 estimated by power iteration on M^T M with M = A_t^{-1} Delta_t. Delta_t is applied matrix-free as Rhat^T (Rhat v) - A_t v so the quantized system is never materialised.
conditioning.comment_solve: A_t^{-1} is applied through a Cholesky factor of the exact regularized Gram, recomputed once per task. A_t is symmetric positive definite so A_t^{-T} = A_t^{-1}.

gates.comment_replay: The local factor error is a property of the replay, so reproducing M7's recorded value proves this run regenerated the same stream. That is what makes it valid to compare a bound computed here against a weight error recorded there, on any GPU. TF32 is disabled explicitly so an Ampere card cannot silently diverge from the Turing-class arithmetic upstream.
gates.comment_noise_floor: Delta_t is formed as Rhat^T Rhat - A_t, so its rounding error is of order eps_machine * ||A_t||, which after applying A_t^{-1} leaves a floor of about eps_machine * kappa(A_t) on epsilon_t. Below that floor the estimate is arithmetic noise. Run the audit in float64 if a width reports epsilon close to its floor.
gates.comment_bound_gate: The Ridge perturbation bound is only valid when epsilon_t < 1. The decisive scientific gate is that epsilon_t/(1-epsilon_t) is at least the relative weight error recorded by M7 for the same width and task. A violation would indicate an error in the derivation or in the estimator, not a property of the method, and must be reported rather than tuned away.
gates.comment_no_accuracy: M17 measures no accuracy, makes no prediction, opens no test split, and cannot change the status of M6 or M7.
